topic.readerProblem: A site owner deciding "301 vs 302 redirect" needs a straight recommendation and the evidence for it.
topic.connection: The free SEO audit flags exactly this decision on real sites (redirect types, HTTPS, structure, image formats); the page links into it.

sources.supports: 301/308 permanent (show target), 302/307 temporary (show source); server-side redirects most reliable.
Redirects are a strong canonical signal; Google prefers HTTPS over HTTP as canonical.
Google follows up to 10 redirect hops; 4xx except 429 treated the same; 429 and 5xx slow crawling; soft 404.
308 Permanent Redirect preserves the request method.
URL mapping, keep redirects at least 1 year, avoid redirecting many URLs to the homepage (soft 404), Change of Address.

artifacts.description: AEOeye Technical SEO Baseline (391 sites, 2026-10-24) — the raw data behind the figures quoted in this decision page.

methodology: Figures come from AEOeye's own zero-cost measurements published under /resources: plain HTTP requests from a self-identified research user agent (AEOeyeResearch), robots.txt respected, 1 s between requests per domain; encoding tests run locally with cwebp/avifenc and SSIM via ffmpeg. Each dataset file states its exact method.
limitations: Convenience sample of well-known sites (not the whole web), homepages only, a single snapshot on 2026-10-24; the image test covers 20 screenshots, not photographs.
